svelteMeasuredOn.note: Svelte coverage (functions/lines over .svelte and .svelte.ts modules) is platform-dependent: Bun instruments the compiled output identically in both environments' coordinates, yet macOS arm64 measures functions in the low-to-mid 80s% / lines in the high-30s% while GitHub Actions' ubuntu-latest (linux x64) measures functions in the mid-70s% / lines in the low-20s%. CI is the authoritative measuring environment, so this floor is pinned to what CI measures, not what a contributor's Mac measures. The prior 0.8134/0.3221 floor (introduced in PR #560, identical to Chat's own svelte floor from the same era) was never verified against this package's own CI run—Cinder was not wired into unit-tests.yaml/main-green.yaml's test:coverage filter until this same change (CIN-604/CIN-605)—so it passed locally on macOS without ever being checked against the Linux number that is now known to fail it. `check-coverage-ratchet.ts` detects when a local run's platform/architecture differs from this record and says so in its output; it never fails a local run for that mismatch alone. IMPORTANT — the CI-measured svelte number is itself NONDETERMINISTIC run-to-run on an unchanged corpus: three independent CI 'package' job runs on this branch, all measuring the identical 291 svelte files (verified via `git diff --stat` across all three commits touching zero .svelte/.svelte.ts files) with a fresh (cache-miss, not cache-replayed) execution of the coverage task each time, printed functions 76.53%/lines 21.07% (job 103436381025 at 67603ed8a, 2026-09-11), functions 76.53%/lines 21.07% (job 103349830223 at 37b4b803f, 2026-09-11), and functions 76.57%/lines 20.97% (job 103583209011 at d9efb50df, 2026-09-12) — the third run FAILED the previous floor that had been pinned to the first two runs' exact number. Bun version, turbo-cache replay, build state, NODE_ENV compile mode, and svelte-source drift were each ruled out as the cause; the remaining candidate is nondeterministic instrumentation/aggregation inside Bun's coverage collector itself (e.g. worker/thread scheduling affecting which code paths execute coverage-instrumented setup vs. cached compiled output), not a real change in what the tests exercise. A ratchet pinned to one exact nondeterministic sample is a flaky gate by construction, so this floor instead carries a deliberate margin sized off the observed variance (functions swung 0.04pt across the 3 samples, 76.53-76.57; lines swung 0.10pt, 20.97-21.07): functions 0.75 sits 1.53pt below the observed minimum (76.53%), about 38x the observed functions swing, and tolerates roughly 6 new svelte files landing at zero measured coverage before tripping; lines 0.199 sits 1.07pt below the observed minimum (20.97%), about 10.7x the observed lines swing, and tolerates roughly 15 new svelte files at zero coverage. Both margins are sized to comfortably absorb several repeats of the observed run-to-run swing plus modest denominator drift from new files, while still catching a genuine collapse in svelte coverage. Consequently this floor is a catastrophic-regression detector, not a fine-grained ratchet: do NOT re-pin it to a single CI run's exact printed number the way the previous round did — that is what caused this failure. Anyone raising this floor later must re-derive the margin from freshly observed run-to-run variance (several CI samples on an unchanged svelte corpus), not just move it to match the latest single measurement.
